d1DesignDecision: A route-less denial prints exactly two lines. Line 1 is identical in both cases and states the fact without overclaiming: 'No human override route is offered for this exact <subject>; the guard attempted to plan one.' -- 'offered' rather than 'available', because for author-repair-required a route does exist through the CLI with an explicit --author-source-root; the guard simply does not offer one. Line 2 distinguishes the two outcomes, because they mean different things: a non-planned status is the planner ANSWERING ('Reason: the override planner returned status=<status>[, code=<code>] (<clause>).'), a throw is the planner being unable to answer ('Reason: planning the route failed with code=<code>.'). Every token is read off the observed outcome; the per-status clause is a fixed map keyed on the observed status, and a status with no entry is still reported, just without a clause -- nothing is guessed. Disclosure is bounded by construction, not by care: status, code and subject are each rendered only if they match a typed-token shape and are <= 64 bytes, so no path separator, whitespace, newline or colon can pass; candidateSourceRoot (the one absolute host path a non-planned outcome carries) is never read; error.message and error.stack are never read.
